_meta.indication: CAPLYTA is indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with active comparator
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled with active comparator; arms lumateperone 42 mg, lumateperone 84 mg, risperidone 4 mg, placebo daily; 4 weeks inpatient treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 4 on PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.result: Lumateperone 42 mg was statistically superior to placebo on PANSS total score change (placebo-subtracted difference -5.8; 95% CI -10.5, -1.1); unadjusted two-sided p=0.017 (multiplicity adjusted 0.034)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; arms lumateperone 28 mg, lumateperone 42 mg, placebo daily; 4 weeks inpatient treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 4 on PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.result: Lumateperone 42 mg was statistically superior to placebo on PANSS total score change (placebo-subtracted difference -4.2; 95% CI -7.8, -0.6); unadjusted two-sided p=0.022 (multiplicity adjusted 0.045)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and greater than twice placebo) were somnolence/sedation (24% vs 10% placebo) and dry mouth (6% vs 2%); other AEs included nausea 9% and dizziness 5%
target_moa: Mechanism in schizophrenia is unknown but efficacy may be mediated through antagonist activity at central serotonin 5-HT2A receptors and postsynaptic antagonist activity at central dopamine D2 receptors
modality: Small molecule (new molecular entity atypical antipsychotic)

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs; CAPLYTA is not approved for dementia-related psychosis

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee Meeting was originally scheduled for July 31, 2019 but was cancelled after the Applicant filed a Major Amendment; no vote was taken

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for an update to Section 14 of the Prescribing Information, specifically to add the results from a study completed in response to Post-Marketing Commitment (PMC) 3760-7 to conduct a placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal maintenance study of lumateperone in patients with schizophrenia.

basis.text: Lumateperone was granted Fast Track Designation in 2017, based on the premise that it is better tolerated than approved drugs for schizophrenia

citations.quote: Lumateperone was granted Fast Track Designation in 2017.

In September 2017, the Applicant submitted requests for both Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy Designations, based on the premise that lumateperone is better-tolerated than approved drugs for the treatment of schizophrenia.

summary.text: Lumateperone was submitted via the 505(b)(1) pathway for schizophrenia in adults and was granted Fast Track Designation in 2017, which supported a rolling review; the Breakthrough Therapy request was denied over nonclinical safety concerns. A planned Advisory Committee Meeting was cancelled after a Major Amendment extended the goal date, and the NDA was approved December 27, 2019.

citations.quote: Intra-Cellular Therapies, Inc. (ITI) is seeking approval of lumateperone for the treatment of schizophrenia in adult patients via the 505b (1) pathway.
The application was granted a rolling review based on the program's Fast Track designation.
